detail.longDescription: arXiv:2611.33736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating dialogue of a population with LLM-enacted personas is increasingly common, yet each pipeline is generally built for one task, so a new task usually means reworking how the persona is authored, enacted and evaluated. We present an end-to-end persona dialogue pipeline meant to carry over to other populations as a whole; a background is written by an LLM from a national survey report, an off-the-shelf LLM enacts it without fine-tuning, and both are rated for perceived plausibility. We apply it to thirty personas of Korean older adults living alone; three LLM judges compare eight simulator LLMs, and thirty experts who work with this population evaluate the selected one, GPT-5.5. Experts found the backgrounds and dialogues largely realistic but most often faulted a persona for being more capable than its background said, and agreement between their ratings and the LLM judges could not be established. We release the pipeline, personas and their dialogues.
